{{Infobox ancient site|location={{ill|Nara (city)|qid=Q169134}}|part_of={{ill|Gosashi Kofun|qid=Q5587136}}; {{ill|Hishage Kofun|qid=Q11330004}}; {{ill|Ichiniwa Kofun|qid=Q11480471}}; {{ill|Konabe Kofun|qid=Q11302279}}; {{ill|Maezuka Kofun|qid=Q11339900}}; {{ill|Saki Hyōtanyama Kofun|qid=Q11383488}}; {{ill|Saki Ishizukayama Kofun|qid=Q11383491}}; {{ill|Saki Misasagiyama Kofun|qid=Q11383490}}; {{ill|Saki Takatsuka Kofun|qid=Q27898021}}; {{ill|Shiozuka Kofun|qid=Q11428650}}; {{ill|Uwanabe Kofun|qid=Q11289362}}; {{ill|Yomondo Maruzuka Kofun|qid=Q11626337}}}}
'''Saki Tatenami Kofun Group''' (佐紀盾列古墳群)<ref>Some sources read this as "Saki Tatami" ([http://www.kashikoken.jp/museum/yamatonoiseki/kofun/sakimisasagiyama.html Kashihara Archaeological Institute website], etc.).</ref> is a kofun group located in the northwestern part of {{ill|Nara (city)|en|Nara (city)|qid=Q169134|lt=Nara City}}, on the southwestern slopes of the {{ill|Nara Hills|ja|奈良丘陵}}, west of the {{ill|Saho River|ja|佐保川}}. Constructed during the late Early to Middle {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}}, it includes many royal tombs associated with the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|ja_comment=|2=ja|3=ヤマト王権|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2658252}}.

== Overview ==

[[File:Sakitatenami kohungun aerial 2.jpg|thumb|300px|{{ill|Gosashi Kofun|ja|五社神古墳}} (top left), {{ill|Saki Ishizukayama Kofun|ja|佐紀石塚山古墳}} (bottom center), {{ill|Saki Misasagiyama Kofun|ja|佐紀陵山古墳}} (bottom right), and {{ill|Saki Takatsuka Kofun|ja|佐紀高塚古墳}} (bottom) ({{National Air Photograph}})]]
[[File:Sakitatenami kohungun aerial 1.jpg|thumb|300px|{{ill|Hishage Kofun|ja|ヒシアゲ古墳|lt=Hishiage Kofun}} (top left), {{ill|Konabe Kofun|ja|コナベ古墳}} (bottom center), and {{ill|Uwanabe Kofun|ja|ウワナベ古墳}} (bottom right) ({{National Air Photograph}})]]
[[File:Yodo River and Yamato River Basins.svg|300px|thumb|right|Geographical relationships of the Saki Tatenami Kofun Group and other kofun groups]]

The kofun group, situated on the southern slopes of the {{ill|Narayama Hills|ja|佐紀丘陵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saki Hills|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 平城山丘陵|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11482305}}, was actively used during the late 4th to early 5th century, spanning the late Early to Middle Kofun period. The group includes three colossal keyhole-shaped kofun from the late Early period and four more from the Middle period. These are likely royal tombs of the early {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|ja_comment=|2=ja|3=ヤマト王権|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2658252}}.

During this era, the Yamato Kingship transitioned from the {{ill|Makimuku Kofun Cluster|ja|纏向古墳群|lt=Makimuku Kofun Group}} and {{ill|Yanagimoto Kofun Cluster|ja|柳本古墳群|lt=Yamato-Yanagimoto Kofun Group}}, located in the southeastern Nara Basin, to the Saki Tatenami Kofun Group, which saw the construction of massive kofun. However, by the late Middle period in the late 5th century, the group declined.

The kofun in this group are characterized by keyhole-shaped mounds without distinct paddle-shaped frontal sections.

== Origin of the Name ==

The name originates from the designations of two prominent kofun: {{ill|Gosashi Kofun|ja|五社神古墳}} and {{ill|Saki Ishizukayama Kofun|ja|佐紀石塚山古墳}}, both identified by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ar|وكالة رعاية القصر الإمبراطوري|ca|Agència de la Casa Imperial|de|Kaiserliches Hofamt|es|Agencia de la Casa Imperial|fa|دفتر خاندان امپراتوری|fr|Agence impériale|ha|Hukumar Kula da Gidajen Daular|he|סוכנות משק הבית הקיסרי|hr|Uprava japanskog carskog dvora|id|Badan Rumah Tangga Kekaisaran|it|Agenzia della Casa Imperiale|ja|宮内庁|ko|일본 궁내청|lt|Imperatoriškosios šeimos agentūra|min|Badan Rumah Tanggo Kakaisaran|ms|Agensi Rumah Tangga Imperial|nl|Japans hof|pl|Agencja Dworu Cesarskiego|pt|Agência da Casa Imperial|ru|Управление Императорского двора Японии|simple|Imperial Household Agency|th|สำนักพระราชวังหลวง (ญี่ปุ่น)|tr|İmparatorluk Sarayı Ajansı|uk|Управління Імператорського двору Японії|vi|Cơ quan nội chính Hoàng gia Nhật Bản|zh|宫内厅|qid=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} as "Saki Tatenami Mausolea."<ref>For example, the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ace|Kojiki|ar|كوجيكي|az|Kociki|bcl|Kojiki|be|Кодзікі|bg|Коджики|ca|Kojiki|ckb|کۆجیکی|cs|Kodžiki|da|Kojiki|de|Kojiki|eo|Koĝiki|es|Kojiki|et|Kojiki|eu|Kojiki|fa|کوجیکی|fi|Kojiki|fr|Kojiki|gl|Kojiki|he|קוג'יקי|hi|कोजिकी|hr|Kojiki|hu|Kodzsiki|hy|Կոձիկի|id|Kojiki|it|Kojiki|ja|古事記|ka|კოძიკი|kk|Кодзики|kn|ಕೋಜಿಕಿ|ko|고사기|la|Kojiki|lt|Kodžiki|mk|Коџики|ml|കൊജികി|ms|Kojiki|my|ခိုဂျိခိ|nl|Kojiki|no|Kojiki|oc|Kojiki|pl|Kojiki|pt|Kojiki|ro|Kojiki|rsk|Кодїки|ru|Кодзики|sh|Kojiki|simple|Kojiki|sk|Kodžiki|sl|Kodžiki|sr|Коџики|sv|Kojiki|ta|கோஜிகி|th|โคจิกิ|tl|Kojiki|tr|Kojiki|uk|Кодзікі|vi|Cổ sự ký|zh|古事記|zh_classical|古事記|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}}'' describes Emperor Seimu's tomb as being "in Saki Tatami," while the ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}'' specifies "buried in the Saki Tatenami Mausoleum."</ref>

The term "Tatenami" (盾列, "shield alignment") may refer to the shield-like layout of the moats surrounding the keyhole-shaped kofun, which are aligned in a north-south direction with the circular rear mounds to the north and the rectangular frontal sections to the south. It likely developed as a descriptive term after the establishment of {{ill|Heijō-kyō|cs|Heidžó-kjó|de|Heijō-kyō|es|Heijō-kyō|eu|Heijo-kyo|fa|هیجو-کیو|fi|Heijō-kyō|fr|Heijō-kyō|gor|Heijō-kyō|hu|Heidzsó-kjó|id|Heijō-kyō|it|Heijō-kyō|ja|平城京|ko|헤이조쿄|la|Heijō-kyō|min|Heijō-kyō|ms|Heijō-kyō|pl|Heijō-kyō|pt|Heijō-kyō|ru|Хэйдзё-кё|sh|Heijō-kyō|simple|Heijō-kyō|sl|Heidžo-kjo|th|เฮโจเกียว|tr|Heijō-kyō|uk|Хейдзьо-кьо|vi|Heijō-kyō|wuu|平城京|zh|平城京|zh_classical|平城京|zh_yue|平城京|qid=Q862509|lt=Heijō-kyō}}.

Some institutions, such as the {{ill|The Museum, Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Nara Prefecture|de|Museum des Archäologischen Forschungsinstituts der Präfektur Nara in Kashihara|ja|奈良県立橿原考古学研究所附属博物館|qid=Q112961122|lt=Kashihara Archaeological Institute}}, use the historical name "Saki Kofun Group."

== Major Kofun ==

; Northwestern Area (Yamamori-cho)
* {{ill|Gosashi Kofun|ja|五社神古墳}} (identified as the tomb of {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|qid=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū}}, 276 m, late Early Kofun period)

; Western Area (Yamamori-cho, Saki-cho)
* {{ill|Saki Ishizukayama Kofun|ja|佐紀石塚山古墳}} (identified as the tomb of {{ill|Emperor Seimu|en|Emperor Seimu|qid=Q316672|lt=Emperor Seimu}}, 220 m, late Early Kofun period)
* {{ill|Saki Misasagiyama Kofun|ja|佐紀陵山古墳}} (identified as the tomb of {{ill|Hibasu-hime|ja|日葉酢媛命}}, consort of Emperor Suinin, 210 m, late Early Kofun period)
* {{ill|Saki Takatsuka Kofun|ja|佐紀高塚古墳}} (associated with {{ill|Empress Kōken|ja|称徳天皇|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress Kōken|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 孝謙天皇|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q232955}}, direction of frontal section unknown)

; Eastern Area (Saki-cho, Hokkeji-cho)
* {{ill|Hishage Kofun|ja|ヒシアゲ古墳|lt=Hishiage Kofun}} (identified as the tomb of {{ill|Princess Iwa|es|Princesa Iwa|fa|شاهدخت ایوا|fr|Impératrice Iwa no hime|ja|磐之媛命|ko|이와노히메노미코토|ru|Ива-но химэ|th|เจ้าหญิงอิวะ|uk|Принцеса Іва|vi|Iwa no Hime|zh|磐之媛命|qid=Q1066593}}, 218 m, Middle Kofun period)
* {{ill|Konabe Kofun|ja|コナベ古墳}} (204 m, Middle Kofun period)
* {{ill|Uwanabe Kofun|ja|ウワナベ古墳}} (265 m, Middle Kofun period)

==Merged second translation==
'''Saki Tatenami Kofun Group''' (佐紀盾列古墳群, *Saki Tatenami Kofungun*)<ref>Some references read it as "Saki Tatanami" (e.g., [http://www.kashikoken.jp/museum/yamatonoiseki/kofun/sakimisasagiyama.html Kashihara Archaeological Institute website]).</ref> is a kofun (ancient Kofun) group located in the northwest area of {{ill|Nara (city)|en|Nara (city)|qid=Q169134|lt=Nara}}, on the southwestern slopes of the Nara Hills along the west bank of the Saho River. It includes many royal tombs from the late {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}}, managed by the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|ja_comment=|2=ja|3=ヤマト王権|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2658252}}. The group is also referred to as the '''Saki Kofun Group'''.

== Overview ==
[[File:Sakitatenami kohungun aerial 2.jpg|thumb|300px|[[Gosashi Kofun]] (top left), [[Saki Ishizukayama Kofun]] (bottom center), [[Saki Misasagiyama Kofun]] (bottom right), and [[Saki Takatsuka Kofun]] (bottom) ({{国土航空写真}})]]
[[File:Sakitatenami kohungun aerial 1.jpg|thumb|300px|[[Hishage Kofun]] (top left), [[Konabe Kofun]] (bottom center), and [[Uwanabe Kofun]] (bottom right) ({{国土航空写真}})]]
[[File:Yodo River and Yamato River Basins.svg|300px|thumb|right|Saki Tatenami Kofun Group and other kofun groups in the region]]
The kofun in this group were built along the southern slopes of the {{ill|Narayama Hills|ja|佐紀丘陵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saki Hills|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 平城山丘陵|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11482305}} from the latter half of the early Kofun period through the middle Kofun period (late 4th century to early 5th century). The group contains numerous large {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|ko|전방후원분|simple|Zenpō-kōen-fun|zh|前方後圓墳|qid=Q11268718|lt=Zenpō-kōen-fun}} (keyhole-shaped Kofuns), including three from the late early period and four from the middle period. These mounds are likely the royal tombs of the early Yamato Kingship.

While earlier Kofuns, such as those in the {{ill|Makimuku Kofun Cluster|ja|纏向古墳群|lt=Makimuku Kofun Group}} and the {{ill|Yanagimoto Kofun Cluster|ja|大和・柳本古墳群|lt=Yamato-Yanagimoto Kofun Group}}, are associated with the establishment of the Yamato Kingship, they declined by the early 5th century. During the late 4th to early 5th centuries, this kofun group became the center for building large royal tombs. However, by the late 5th century, the group's prominence diminished.

The kofun in this group exhibit unique characteristics, such as keyhole-shaped mounds with less pronounced plectrum-like front sections.

== Etymology ==
The name "Saki Tatenami" comes from the designation of two representative tombs, "Gosashi Kofun" and "Saki Ishizukayama Kofun," both identified as "狭城盾列陵" (*Saki Tatenami no Misasagi*) in historical records.<ref>The *Kojiki* records the tomb of Emperor Seimu as being "at Saki's Tatanami," while the *Nihon Shoki* refers to it as "at Saki's Tatenami." Similarly, the tomb of Empress Jingū is recorded in the *Nihon Shoki* as being at "Saki's Tatenami no Misasagi."</ref>

The term "Tate-nami" (盾列, shield row) is thought to describe the shield-shaped layout of the mounds, with parallel orientations: the rear circular sections (kōen) are to the north, and the frontal rectangular sections (zenpō) are to the south. This name likely emerged during or after the Nara period.

The {{ill|The Museum, Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Nara Prefecture|de|Museum des Archäologischen Forschungsinstituts der Präfektur Nara in Kashihara|ja|奈良県立橿原考古学研究所附属博物館|qid=Q112961122|lt=Kashihara Archaeological Institute}} uses the more simplified term "Saki Kofun Group," based solely on the geographical area.

== Notable Kofun ==

=== Northwestern Section (Sanryō-chō) ===
* {{ill|Gosashi Kofun|ja|五社神古墳}} (276 meters, late early period, attributed to Empress Jingū)  
  Researchers were granted partial access to the first tier of the mound in 2008.

=== Western Section (Sanryō-chō/Saki-chō) ===
* {{ill|Saki Ishizukayama Kofun|ja|佐紀石塚山古墳}} (220 meters, late early period, attributed to Emperor Seimu)  
* {{ill|Saki Misasagiyama Kofun|ja|佐紀陵山古墳}} (210 meters, late early period, attributed to Empress Hibasu-hime)  
  Stone structures and paving were identified in the rear circular mound.  
* Saki Takatsuka Kofun  
* {{ill|Saki Hyōtanyama Kofun|en|Saki Hyōtanyama Kofun|qid=Q11383488|lt=Saki Hyōtan-yama Kofun}} (96 meters, designated as a National Historic Site in 1971)

=== Eastern Section (Saki-chō/Hokkera-chō) ===
* {{ill|Hishage Kofun|ja|ヒシアゲ古墳}} (218 meters, middle period, attributed to Empress Iwanohime)  
* {{ill|Konabe Kofun|ja|コナベ古墳}} (204 meters, middle period)  
* {{ill|Uwanabe Kofun|ja|ウワナベ古墳}} (265 meters, middle period)

=== Northern Section (Utahime-chō) ===
* {{ill|Shiozuka Kofun|en|Shiozuka Kofun|qid=Q11428650|lt=Shiotsuka Kofun}} (109 meters, middle period)  
  Designated as a National Historic Site in 1975.  

=== Related Kofun ===
* {{ill|Hōraiyama Kofun|ja|宝来山古墳|qid=Q11452574}} (227 meters, attributed to Emperor Suinin)  
  Although geographically outside the Saki area, this kofun is administratively grouped with the Saki Tatenami Kofun Group by the Imperial Household Agency.
